transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Hi. Yeah, thank you. Um, well, it's kind of a long story, but I guess the main reason I'm here is because... well, my behavior has just been really extreme lately, I guess? 

I recently moved, and for a bit, I was barely settling into my new apartment. Like, just completely stalled out, staring at boxes in the living room for days, not really doing anything. But then, out of nowhere, it was like I suddenly had to fix my entire life in one giant sprint. I'm a digital interface designer, so I guess my brain just went into full agile project-management mode, but on absolute overdrive. 

I went from doing the bare minimum to suddenly saying yes to all these junior designer mentoring sessions—which, you know, take up hours of prep time and emotional energy—and on top of that, I started taking on all these extra client prototypes at work. Just volunteering for the most complicated wireframing projects we had. And if that wasn't enough, I decided I absolutely needed to completely redesign my whole portfolio from scratch right then and there. Every single pixel, rewriting every case study, tweaking the UI until my eyes hurt. 

It was just this sudden, massive avalanche of taking things on. I just kept adding to the list, taking on more and more, because I felt this intense need to tackle all these massive career and life goals at the exact same time. And it's just... I don't know, I'm looking around at everything I've committed to, and I realize going from zero to a hundred like that, trying to overhaul my entire existence in a week, isn't exactly a normal way to operate. So... yeah, that's what brought me in.
Have you experienced episodes like this before, where you suddenly take on a huge amount of projects or feel driven to accomplish a lot in a short time?

Um, well, it's hard to say for sure, honestly. I mean, I'm trying to think back... I guess I've always been someone who throws themselves into their work, you know? Like, in the tech world, there's always this pressure to be constantly updating your skills, learning the newest prototyping tools, keeping up with the latest UX trends... so it's kind of baked into the culture to just grind and take on a lot. 

But as for this specific feeling... this kind of sudden, overwhelming compulsion to just do *everything* all at once? I don't know. I mean, maybe? I'm trying to think if there was another time I felt exactly like this, where I went from completely stalled out to just... hyper-speed. It's tough to untangle what's just me being a perfectionist designer and what's... whatever this is. 

Like, there was this one time a couple of years ago when we were launching a major app redesign, and I definitely worked some crazy hours, but that felt more driven by external deadlines, you know? Not this weird internal pressure I'm feeling right now, where I'm the one piling the work on myself for no real reason. So, I don't know, maybe I haven't? Or maybe I have and I just didn't realize it was a pattern? It's just all really confusing to look back on right now.

During this time when you were taking on so much work and redesigning your portfolio, did you feel unusually energetic, as if you didn’t need much sleep, or like your thoughts were racing faster than usual?

Yeah, actually, the sleep thing... that was probably the weirdest part of it all. Because normally, I am someone who absolutely needs a solid seven or eight hours. If I don't get that, I'm usually just a total zombie staring blankly at my monitor all day, completely useless. 

But during this whole... whatever this was, this massive productivity sprint... it was completely different. For several nights, I think maybe four or five nights in a row, I was getting maybe three or four hours of sleep, tops. I'd be up until 2 or 3 AM just obsessing over the typography on my portfolio or reorganizing my entire file structure, and then my eyes would just snap open at 6 AM. 

And the crazy part is, I didn't feel tired at all. You'd think after three hours of sleep I'd feel like I got hit by a bus, but I would wake up convinced I was totally fine. More than fine, really. I felt this incredible surge of energy, and my brain would instantly start running through my to-do list, just racing through all the things I could accomplish. It was like my thoughts were moving at lightspeed the second I opened my eyes. 

I remember just lying there in the dark for maybe a minute, thinking, well, I'm awake, I feel perfectly rested, I should really just use this extra time to get ahead on things. So I'd literally just roll out of bed, make a pour-over coffee, and dive right back into prepping for those junior mentoring sessions or tweaking UI components before the sun was even up. It felt like I had unlocked this secret cheat code for extra hours in the day, and sleep just seemed... I don't know, like a complete waste of time when I had so much momentum going. I just didn't want to stop. So yeah, the energy was definitely way, way higher than normal, and my brain was just constantly buzzing with the next thing I needed to do.
During this time of increased energy and productivity, did you feel unusually upbeat, overly confident, or maybe even a little irritable — like you were on top of the world or couldn’t be stopped?

Yeah, that's... that's a really good way to put it, actually. It was this weird mix of both. Earlier this month, when all this was happening, I definitely felt this intense, almost electric kind of upbeat energy. Like I was completely dialed in and everything I was doing was just brilliant. I remember looking at the new wireframes I was building and thinking, "Wow, this is the best work I've ever done in my entire career, I am absolutely nailing this." I felt so capable, you know? Like nothing could slow me down and I was just operating on this entirely different, superior level. 

But then... the flip side of that was the irritability. Oh my god, the irritability. Because I felt like I was moving so fast and being so incredibly productive, anyone who wasn't matching my pace—which was literally everyone, because I was going a million miles an hour—just drove me absolutely insane. 

Like, I was waiting on some assets from this freelance illustrator we use, just a few vector files, and he was maybe an hour late delivering them. Normally, whatever, people get busy, I'd just work on something else. But in that moment? I completely lost it. I sent him this incredibly passive-aggressive, bordering on just aggressive, Slack message. I felt like he was intentionally trying to sabotage my momentum. And then later that same day, my sister texted me asking if I wanted to get dinner later in the week, and she didn't respond to my follow-up text for like twenty minutes, and I actually called her and snapped at her. Over dinner plans! I was just so keyed up, it felt like any tiny delay, any little roadblock, was this massive personal insult. It was like I was on top of the world, but only as long as everyone else stayed exactly out of my way. If they didn't, I just had zero patience. None.
